item.title: Claude Agent SDK
item.description:
Simple definition#

The Claude Agent SDK is Claude Code as a library. From Python or TypeScript you call query(), and the SDK runs the same agent loop, built-in tools (read, edit, shell, search, web), permissions, sessions, hooks, sub-agents and MCP support that power the Claude Code CLI — inside a process you operate. You supply the prompt, the tools it may use, and callbacks that decide what it’s allowed to do.

item.title: The Enterprise AI Stack: Reference Architecture
item.description:
Simple definition#

The enterprise AI stack is the set of shared layers an organisation builds so that many teams can ship AI features safely and cheaply: access to models, a gateway to control that access, pipelines that turn company data into retrievable knowledge, frameworks for chains and agents, and the operations, security and governance around all of it.

item.title: AI Engineering Architecture: Building It Up Step by Step
item.description:
Simple definition#

Most AI applications converge on the same architecture, but no team should build it all on day one. This article grows it one component at a time, each added only when a concrete need appears: context, guardrails, routing, caching, actions — and the observability that makes all of it operable.

item.title: On-Premise and Hybrid GenAI Deployment
item.description:
Simple definition#

Deployment topology decides where each part of a GenAI system runs: the model, the retrieval index, the orchestration code and the logs. On-premise means inference runs on hardware you operate; hybrid means some workloads run on your hardware or private cloud and others call cloud-hosted models, with one control plane deciding which request goes where.

item.title: Hybrid AI in Financial Services: Practical Decisions
item.description:
Simple definition#

In financial services, hybrid AI means running each AI workload in the place its data, regulation and economics allow: frontier models through in-region cloud for tasks that need the best reasoning, open-weight or licensed models on the bank’s own infrastructure for restricted data and high-volume work, and one governed control plane across both.
